groups.label: Curriculum and Philosopher Education
groups.summary: These commentaries detail the philosopher-guardian's ascent from arithmetic, geometry, and motion sciences to dialectic and the apprehension of the Good. They evaluate the full lifespan schema, the pedagogical turning of the soul, and the epistemological contrasts between theoretical abstraction and practical civic administration.
groups.rationale: All seven nodes share Theme 5 and derive from introductory commentaries examining the curriculum, developmental schedule, and epistemological goals of education in the Republic.

groups.label: Commentary on Democratic Decay and Tyranny
groups.summary: These analyses explore the societal shift from oligarchic wealth accumulation to democratic excess, which inevitably spawns tyrannical dominance. They trace the psychological descent into lawless appetites and expose the utter misery and enslavement experienced by the tyrannical ruler.
groups.rationale: These entries form a cohesive sequence of thematic commentary (Theme 6) covering the decline of democracy into tyranny and the pathological psychology of the tyrant.

groups.label: Dialogue on Democracy and Tyranny
groups.summary: In Book VIII dialogue passages, Socrates details how popular revolt establishes democratic freedom, diversity, and shifting individual desires. He then explains how extreme license destabilizes the three civic classes, allowing an ambitious protector to purge rivals, seize absolute power, and brutally enslave the city.
groups.rationale: These seven nodes encompass the primary dialogue occurrences from Book VIII outlining the genesis of democracy, its structural decay, and the emergence of the tyrant.
